Jordan / team —

Quick legal summary and suggested edits (high level):

• Auto-renew: MSA currently defaults to a single renewal term equal to the prior term length unless either party provides written notice at least 60 days before the then-current term end. For pilots, we can add an explicit carve-out so pilot agreements terminate at the end of the initial term unless both parties opt-in to renewal. Proposed language: add a new sentence to 4.2: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Pilot Agreements shall not automatically renew unless the Parties execute a written extension prior to the end of the Initial Term."

• Termination for convenience (Order Form): The Order Form contains a termination-for-convenience right for the customer with 30 days' notice. Operational risk centers on data/export windows and third-party billing. We recommend: 1) 30 days' notice standard; 2) a 45-day data export window in the event of termination for convenience for accounts that store artifacts longer than standard retention; 3) a one-time transition assistance fee (if customer requests active migration support beyond exports) — optional commercial add-on. Redline summary attached.

• Third-party integrations: Add a single sentence clarifying that Redwood is not liable for third-party pass-through costs after termination and will provide reasonable cooperation for transferring any third-party subscriptions, with customer responsible for third-party charges.

I attached a tracked-changes MSA redline and a short "off-ramp checklist" ops doc for Aditya to review.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Samantha —

Appreciate the questions and the redline. Quick summary of where we landed internally and next steps so procurement has a single doc to review: 

1) Auto-renew: We will add explicit pilot carve-out language so pilots do not auto-renew unless both parties agree in writing. Standard paid contracts will continue to auto-renew absent 60 days' notice.

2) Termination for convenience: We will keep customer T4C with 30 days' notice on the Order Form. We'll add a 45-day data export window for accounts with artifacts beyond our standard retention and include an optional transition assistance service (one-time fee) if Acme wants active migration help.

3) Third-party billing and liability: We'll include a sentence stating Redwood isn't responsible for third-party pass-through costs post-termination and will cooperate reasonably to transfer services to Acme.

Attached: finalized redline (ACME_MSA_redline_20270420.docx) and the off-ramp checklist in PDF. If this aligns with Acme's procurement needs I can route the MSA + Order Form for signature via DocuSign (link below) and propose a 30-day DocuSign turnaround to meet your timeline.
